meta.question: What Defines the SAP system landscape?

question: What Defines the SAP system landscape?

answers:
The SAP systems within a landscape have specific requirements concerning servers, operating systems, network configurations, and supported storage. Your business and functional needs will dictate the SAP solutions that utilize either the SAP HANA Database Server or the SAP NetWeaver Application Server, thereby influencing how your applications interact with the available infrastructure.
Your requirements also play a crucial role in determining how to size your servers. You have a wide selection of SAP NetWeaver-based applications to choose from, which may include SAP HANA. This includes options like SAP S/4HANA, SAP ERP Central Component (ECC), SAP BW/4HANA, SAP BW, and many more solutions tailored to different business operations.
.

SAP HANA (High-Performance Analytic Appliance) is a multi-model database that stores data in memory rather than on disk. This configuration allows for data processing that is significantly faster than that of traditional disk-based systems, enabling advanced real-time analytics. An SAP HANA system is identified by a single system ID (SID) and includes one or more tenant databases as well as one system database. Each database is identified by its SID and a database name. The SAP systems in a landscape have specific requirements for servers, operating systems, network configurations, and supported storage options.
What are the hardware and software requirements for SAP HANA?

The hardware and software requirements for SAP HANA are described in the SAP HANA Master Guide, which can be found at this link: <https://help.sap.com/viewer/eb3777d5495d46c5b2fa773206bbfb46/2.0.01/en-US/d3d1cf20bb5710149b57fd794c827a4e.html>. Additionally, the certified and supported SAP HANA hardware for SAP-certified Cloud IaaS platforms can be found here: <https://www.sap.com/dmc/exp/2014-09-02-hana-hardware/enEN//solutions?filters=iaas;ve:28>. SAP HANA and SAP NetWeaver on UNIX/Linux are also supported.

evidence.text:
Determining your SAP applications 

An SAP landscape is a group of two or more SAP Systems that usually include development, quality and test, and production.

One SAP System consists of one or more SAP instances, which are a group of processes that are started and stopped at the same time. These SAP instances are grouped to form a specified SAP system for a defined use for a region or business unit. Then, the instances are grouped in a landscape as development, test, or production SAP Systems with one or multiple tracks (such as "project" and "business"). This landscape design is up to each business, dependent on business requirements.

Define your SAP system landscape 

Your business and functional requirements determine the SAP solutions powered by the SAP HANA Database Server or SAP NetWeaver Application Server, and therefore determine how your applications are run the infrastructure available.

Your requirements have an influence on how you size your server. You have a wide selection of SAP NetWeaver-based applications (which may use SAP HANA) to choose from, including SAP S/4HANA, SAP ERP Central Component (ECC), SAP BW/4HANA, SAP BW and many more solutions for differnt business operations.

Storage design considerations 

The SAP systems in a landscape have specific requirements for servers, operating systems, network setup, and supported storage.

For SAP workloads that use a Cloud Service Provider, Infrastructure-as-a-Service is similar to existing practices used to run SAP workloads in external data centers or by a data center provider. An SAP landscape has specific requirements for connectivity, between hosts within Cloud IaaS and to external systems. IBM Cloud® for SAP provides a rich set of functions to improve your SAP landscape, beyond hosting SAP systems.

To assist your project's planning phase, the below sections provide IBM Cloud® for SAP portfolio design considerations for Storage.



 Preface: units of measure for data/information 

Storage performance refers to the read/write performance from storage file system. Often the throughput Network Storage is shown in Mbps or Gbps, whereas for Local Disk storage is shown in MiB/s.
